title: Study Journey: Week 1 reflections
text:
This first post captures the start of the Physics 1B study journey.



Fluid mechanics: density, pressure, buoyancy, and fluid flow
Periodic motion: simple harmonic motion, pendulums, and energy in oscillations





Pressure varies with depth: \(P = P_0 + \rho g h\)
Buoyant force equals the weight of displaced fluid
SHM follows the equation \(x(t)=A\cos(\omega t + \phi)\)





Review the derivation of the restoring force for a mass-spring system
Compare the energy exchange between kinetic and potential forms in SHM
Practice applying Bernoulli’s equation to fluid flow problems





Continue weekly posts for each new course topic
Add homework reflections and solution strategies
Use the blog as a review resource before quizzes and exams

Physics for Scientists and Engineers: Oscillations, Waves, Electric and Magnetic Fields

UCLA | Summer Session A6 (6/22 - 7/31)
Instructor: Rossi, G.D.

title: About this Study Journal
text:
📌 About the Course

Enforced requisites: course 1A, Mathematics 31B, 32A.
Enforced corequisite: Mathematics 32B.

Fluid mechanics, oscillation, mechanical waves, and sound. Electric charge, field and potential, capacitors, and dielectrics. Currents and resistance, direct-current circuits. P/NP or letter grading.
The topics covered in this class and approximate schedules are listed below. Chapters listed are from Young and Freedman (Sears and Zemansky’s) University Physics, 14th edition. If a course is taught using the online Kudu textbook, homework, and clicker system, the recommended Kudu course is “UCLA Physics 1B”, which covers the same topics.
